summary: SSE resume hangs when proxy path splits; partial metadata and stalled epilogue on reconnect
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after an intermittent network disruption their SSE streaming response resumes but then stalls: the client receives heartbeat frames and a partial metadata envelope (session_id/seq mismatch) and never receives the final 'end' envelope that marks completion. Impact: NovaDocs users see partial outputs or indefinite streaming hangs for long-running generations (document summarization flows). Roughly 8% of resumed sessions in the last 24h for the customer's dedicated pool show this symptom.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running generation (approx 800-1200 token expected) via SSE against the customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west
2) Force a short connection interruption (simulate NAT timeout / client network swap) during token stream (around 60-120 seconds in),
3) Allow client to reconnect and send the SSE resume token (client uses resume_token header with last_offset),

4) Observe that the resumed stream emits several heartbeat-only chunks, then a metadata envelope with session_id that does not match the pre-drop session, and the final 'end' envelope is not delivered — client parser stays waiting for termination.

comments: 2026-03-10 18:50 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer first reported repeated resumed streams hanging after a CDN path migration. They provided example session IDs and a client-side capture. Customer reports ~8% of resumes failing during their nightly batch runs.

2026-03-10 19:20 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): I pulled edge logs for the customer's pool. I see ConnRebinds to worker-3b and an early CRLF trim from the CDN; sending to runtime to correlate. Assigning to serving-runtime on-call.

2026-03-11 03:05 - Arjun Patel (runtime on-call): Observed that when resume is handled by a different worker the session_id suffix is appended by sidecar rebind code. Parser on client side treats it as mismatched session and drops incoming terminal envelope. Hypothesis: sticky-session not honored for some rebinds under autoscaling.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Provided additional client capture and indicated customer is on Dedicated with autoscaling enabled. Customer requests workaround within 24h to avoid user-facing failures.

2026-03-12 11:43 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied: pinned sticky session policy for NovaDocs dedicated pool for us-west. Also asked them to enable websocket fallback in their client as a short-term change. Monitoring for reduction in failures.

2026-03-13 08:00 - Arjun Patel (runtime): Reproducer added to CI and a fix (avoid appending rebind suffix to session_id) landed in PR #5881. Coordinating rollout; planned canary in us-west on 2026-03-14.
2026-03-13 08:30 - NovaDocs (Customer): Confirmed that after sticky pin was applied new resumed sessions appear to complete end-to-end. They will keep websocket fallback active while we roll out fix.
investigation_notes: Edge logs show frequent conn rebinds in same second window as resume attempts; rebind often sends to a worker instance with '-rebind' suffix in session_id assignment.
Fastly/edge performed an aggressive keepalive trim (early-crlf-trim) which appears to cause the connection to be semi-closed before the runtime flusher finalizes the terminal envelope.
Client parser behavior: the client treats any session_id mismatch as a hard desync and will ignore subsequent 'end' envelopes coming with unexpected session_id namespace.
Autoscaling path: when Dedicated pool scales up during high concurrency we observe ephemeral sidecars using different session namespace which is not transparently compatible with resume semantics.

Hypothesis chain: CDN semi-close -> edge rebind -> worker sidecar appends rebind suffix -> runtime emits terminal envelope with new session_id -> client discards terminal envelope because session_id mismatches -> client waits indefinitely.
workaround: 1) Pinned sticky sessions for NovaDocs dedicated pool in us-west (applied 2026-03-12) — this reduced observed failures in our short window of monitoring.
2) Recommended customer enable websocket fallback for critical flows (client-side change). Websocket fallbacks completed full sessions consistently in our tests.
3) If using a CDN with keepalive trimming, increase origin keepalive timeout or disable early CRLF trimming for the affected route.
resolution: Fix in progress: runtime change to preserve canonical session_id across rebinds (do not append ad-hoc suffixes). PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5881 submitted and passing unit+integration tests. Plan: canary rollout in us-west 2026-03-14, monitor 24h, then global rollout if stable.
next_steps: Canary rollout to 10% of us-west traffic on 2026-03-14 by deploying PR #5881
Monitor resumed stream failure rate vs baseline for 24 hours (target: <0.5% of resumes failing)
Coordinate with NovaDocs to revert sticky-pin once canary is green
Add additional telemetry to resume flow: emit resume_token_origin_worker and resume_token_matched boolean to traces
